lesson.text: Quick memory: what is low relief? (A carving that stands out only a little.) Today: pictures made of tiny squares: pixel art.
A screen picture is made of tiny squares of colour called pixels (short for picture elements). Look very closely at a screen and you may see them.
Pixel art is drawn on a grid, one square at a time, and each square gets one colour. Plan the shape first, then fill it in.
Resolution is how many pixels a picture has. A picture 8 pixels wide and 8 tall has 8 × 8 = 64 pixels. More pixels show more detail: compare this circle with the one below.
The same circle with twice as many pixels across and down: 4 times as many pixels, and a rounder edge. In this game's BLOCKY style, every face of a block is pixel art: 16 × 16 = 256 pixels.
Screens don't mix paint: they mix light. Every pixel is made of tiny red, green and blue lights, and red and green light together make yellow!
Pixel art is like older crafts: Roman mosaics made pictures from small tiles, and cross-stitch from stitches on a grid. The first video games used pixel art because computers had very little memory.
Try it in the world: build a pixel picture in your world, one block for each pixel. Build half of a heart or a face, then mirror it to finish it.

exercises.hint: Think of the squares in the heart.
choices: a tiny square of colour in a picture
exercises.explain: A pixel is one tiny square of colour: a picture element.

exercises.prompt: How many pixels does this picture have, empty ones too?
exercises.hint: Count the squares in one row, then the rows, and multiply.
exercises.explain: 5 pixels in a row and 5 rows: 5 × 5 = 25.

exercises.prompt: More pixels can show more detail.
exercises.hint: Compare the two circles in the lesson.
exercises.explain: True: the circle with more pixels has a rounder, smoother edge.

exercises.prompt: Finish the pixel heart: make both halves match, like a mirror.
exercises.hint: Each block needs a twin the same distance from the middle line on the other side.
exercises.explain: Every block on the left gets a twin on the right, the same distance from the middle.

exercises.prompt: A pixel picture is 10 pixels wide and 10 tall. How many pixels does it have?
Red and green light together make which colour?
exercises.hint: Light doesn't mix like paint. Remember the lesson card about screens.
exercises.explain: Red and green light make yellow. (Red and green paint would make a muddy brown!)

exercises.prompt: Which picture has the higher resolution?
exercises.hint: Which one is made of more pixels?
exercises.explain: The circle with 8 × 8 = 64 pixels has more than the one with 4 × 4 = 16: a higher resolution, and a rounder edge.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to what it means.
exercises.explain: A pixel is one square, resolution is how many, a grid holds them, a mosaic is made of tiles.

exercises.prompt: Finish the pixel tree: make both halves match. The middle column is the mirror line.
exercises.hint: Blocks in the middle column are their own twins. Every other block needs a twin on the other side.
exercises.explain: Each block on the left gets a twin on the right, as far from the middle column.

exercises.prompt: A picture is 16 pixels wide and 16 tall. How many pixels does it have?
exercises.explain: 16 × 16 = 256 pixels, like a block face in the BLOCKY style.

exercises.prompt: An artist makes a 12 × 10 pixel picture twice as wide and twice as tall. How many pixels does it have now?
exercises.hint: Work out the new width and height first.

exercises.prompt: Why did the first video games use pixel art?
exercises.hint: Every pixel had to be stored somewhere.
exercises.explain: Computers had very little memory, so pictures had few pixels and each one was planned.

exercises.prompt: A screen makes its colours by mixing paint.
exercises.hint: What is a pixel made of?
exercises.explain: False: screens mix light: tiny red, green and blue lights.

exercises.prompt: Which colours of light make up every pixel on a screen?
exercises.hint: They are not the paint primaries.
exercises.explain: Screens mix red, green and blue light.
